summary: Phase 149O.20L.7L -- HMIC Frozen Source-Scope Amendment for the DeploymentBinding Producer Independent Verification. Verification-only; nothing repaired, migrated, or authorized. Every claim was reconstructed from immutable Git objects and live code, never from 149O.20L.7K's report, counts, digests, or tests. True pre-7K baseline independently resolved as 6f7073cef2fb2ff839a0ad7e8fee641ba2d53a76 (the real first parent of 7K's implementation commit 1c9f4aa722b85cc0ce55d654d7d078354af94886). Section-by-section contract diff over both immutable revisions: only section 17 (HMIC-REQ-050/051/052) and section 41 (attack matrix) changed, section 54 gained only a trailing separator, section 55 was added, nothing was removed; attack rows 1-38 are byte-identical, row 39 is appended, heading and numbering are coherent at 1..39; the v1.3 -> v1.4 minor bump is correct against this contract's own precedent (sections 50/51/53 minor bumps for widenings vs sections 52/54 same-version repairs). Independently re-extracted HMIC-REQ-050's fenced enumeration from the contract document and read the live production tuples: both exactly 30, agreeing entry-for-entry in the same order with identical spelling -- zero divergence. Exact delta: two additions (core/hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py appended to the src/pcae/-relative bucket, scripts/hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py appended to the root-relative bucket), zero removals, relative order of all 28 prior entries preserved (a subsequence, not a prefix). contract_versions independently confirmed at exactly five members and derive_contract_versions returns HBDC-001 = 1.1 from live headers. Both new members independently classified MUST INCLUDE from source behavior rather than analogy: the producer owns create/rotate/revoke decision logic, the idempotency comparison, the fail-closed DuplicateConflictingBindingError branches, the atomic write and the mandatory read-back verification; the admin script owns a real _prompt_confirm operator gate, AuthorityEvidence construction from raw CLI strings, four required=True authority fields, and operation selection. scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py was read and compared as corroboration only. Independent privileged-writer sweep of src/ and scripts/ found no omitted DeploymentBinding writer; scripts/ contains exactly two Python files, both frozen. Independent ast.parse/ast.walk import walk of both new members reproduced the dependency graph exactly (hatp_bootstrap, paths, provenance, repository_identity; stdlib only otherwise) with no importlib/__import__/subprocess/os.system escape hatch. The pcae.core.provenance exclusion was verified from call ordering at the source -- audit runs strictly after the durable write, read-back verification, and lock release -- so it cannot alter binding content. Full authority-path coverage matrix closed with no unaccounted executable component. Digest work in two disposable git worktrees against the real derive_implementation_scope_digest: pre-tree/28-scope d5129ce26c98b595c6583ec2097274d9257c1f73b2b347503f5b66d7286996ca, pre-tree/30-scope 3a74752f504555cb9569fc0b68adfdf122cf8332542aece7b41244e4de2d9e3d, post-tree/28-scope 008762bb64c1558446078d9e5fd825d0cd9926436aba1dfd7882c925b82e1fa2, post-tree/30-scope 65ff8ab06b5cd7feb2505742cfbb112ffd386c5b2cf34c2d7f3446d92afe15b8 (matching the live working-tree value and 7K's reported figure, thereby independently confirmed rather than accepted). The change was decomposed into independent causes -- file bytes already existing (hatp_mandatory_certification.py is itself a frozen member) versus source-membership expansion -- and the contract-identity axis was kept separate: HMIC-001 is not a member of its own frozen set, so the v1.4 document edit does not enter implementation_scope_digest at all. Perturbation results: each new member individually digest-sensitive under the 30-member scope; the identical perturbation invisible under the pre-amendment 28-member scope (the historical gap demonstrated, not asserted); non-member controls (provenance.py, hatp_signing_ceremony.py, commands/init.py) inert; removal of either new member fails closed with FrozenFileDerivationError and no partial digest; symlink substitution rejected under HMIC-REQ-061; bucket order reversal leaves the digest unchanged (HMIC-REQ-056 lexicographic sort confirmed empirically); duplicate membership double-hashes deterministically and is never silently deduplicated (characterized as a latent, caller-unreachable property of the mechanism, unchanged by 7K); all 30 canonical paths safe, unique, existing, regular, non-symlinked. Byte identity proven by Git blob SHA across 6f7073ce / 1c9f4aa7 / HEAD for the producer, the admin script, hatp_bootstrap.py, repository_identity.py, hatp_class_b_conformance.py, both other Class-B verifiers, the four provider files, scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py and HBDC-001; an AST comparison of hatp_mandatory_certification.py shows every function and class body byte-identical with only the two frozen tuples changed -- no derivation logic touched. Agent reachability re-verified whole-tree: zero AST-level imports of the producer anywhere in src/pcae; the only textual occurrences in hatp_mandatory_certification.py are one comment, one tuple entry, and one docstring line; cli.py exposes no deployment-binding surface. Independent regression A/B in two disposable worktrees with identical invocation and a full sorted FAILED/ERROR node-ID diff: 215 failed / 7628 passed pre-7K vs 253 failed / 7614 passed post-7K, exactly 38 net-new and 0 resolved, independently reproducing 7K's 38 -- every one adjudicated by node ID as a historical predecessor-phase identity pin (149O.20K/20K.1/20K.2/20K.3 exactly-28 and 38-attack-row pins; 20L.1A/1B still-v1.3 pins; 20L.3/20L.4 byte-identity-since-phase-entry pins; 20L.7D.8/7D.10/7E exactly-28 and digest-recomputation pins; 20L.7I no-contract-modified pin), three of which were opened and read in full to confirm rather than infer. Zero security, authority, or behavioral regressions. Regression verdict: REGRESSION CLEAN WITH EXPECTED HISTORICAL IDENTITY-PIN MIGRATION; the raw unfiltered fast_green tally at HEAD is red (253 failed / 7614 passed) and is explicitly not claimed green -- 215 of those failures already existed at the pre-7K baseline. FINAL VERDICT: NOT VERIFIED -- CONTRACT REPAIR REQUIRED. The membership decision, its production alignment, its digest binding, its transitive closure, agent unreachability, and the absence of any behavioral change are all independently verified correct and require no change. The verdict is withheld for finding F-7L-1: HMIC-001 v1.4 asserts, inside HMIC-REQ-052 limb (c)'s own requirement body, in section 55.4 (presented as an independently derived result of 7K's own search), and in attack-matrix row 39 clause (a), that no readiness, certification, or activation code path calls verify_class_b_deployment_conformance -- but src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_cutover.py imports it at line 74 and calls it at line 952 inside _assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root, appending class_b_deployment_conformance_satisfies_readiness as the eighth term of the readiness vector that determines ready. That wiring was introduced by Phase 149O.20L.3 (commit e2ccb7a3, HMRC-REQ-086-100) and independently verified by 149O.20L.4, both ancestors of 7K's own phase-entry commit; the claim was true at v1.3 and became false at 149O.20L.3, and 7K reasserted it by citing section 53 rather than re-measuring. Consequence: the scope amendment is more justified, not less -- the Class-B verdict is a live activation-readiness term today -- but a frozen normative document states a false fact, and attack row 39's not-functionally-load-bearing characterization rests only on clauses (b) and (c) (no real DeploymentBinding has ever been created, no HMIC certification exists), both independently reconfirmed true. Secondary finding F-7L-2: HMIC-001 v1.4's Depends on (current, HMIC-unamended) header still reads HBDC-001 v1.0 while HBDC-001 has been v1.1 since Phase 149O.20L.7G -- precisely the defect class of B-149O.20L.1-1 that section 54 already repaired in place for HMRC-001; derive_contract_versions reads live headers and is unaffected. Non-blocking observations recorded unrepaired: F-7L-3 (src/pcae/commands/init.py, the sole production caller of ensure_repository_identity, is not frozen while repository_identity.py is -- pre-existing and outside 7K's declared scope); F-7L-4 (hatp_signing_ceremony.py is a readiness input via dynamic importability but is not frozen -- exclusion defensible since only an import-breaking edit changes the term, which fails closed); F-7L-5 (attack rows 33/34/36/37/38 carry not-yet-operative caveats already stale before 7K); F-7L-6 (7K's sections-0-54-byte-untouched phrasing is imprecise; section 55's own preamble is accurate); F-7L-7 (the two amended 7I/7J guards exempt hatp_mandatory_certification.py at file granularity in a textual search, so a genuine import added to that module would escape them -- this phase adds a strictly stronger AST-level guard with no per-file exemption as its own artifact, repairing nothing). 7J section 31 finding (canonical reference: 149O.20L.7J section 31 HMIC frozen-source-membership finding; no separate alphanumeric ID exists in 7J's artifacts): REPAIR VERIFIED AT THE MEMBERSHIP/DIGEST LAYER BUT FINDING NOT CLOSED -- the source-scope closure is independently complete, yet the amendment carrying it requires repair before it may be relied upon. HMIC-REQ-103's revocation-does-not-invalidate-existing-validation gap, 7J section 17's audit-failure-after-mutation exception-type gap, hatp_bootstrap.py::_parse_iso_timestamp's permissive-parser finding, and HMIC-REQ-063's import-shadowing/executed-code limitation are all carried forward unchanged and byte-untouched; nothing here claims digest membership proves executed runtime provenance. W-1, B-149O.19.3-1, B-149O.20D-1 and CBV-S1 independently re-confirmed still closed/bound with no regression. Current Mac source candidate after 7L finalization: this phase's own HEAD -- recorded as bookkeeping, explicitly NOT authorized for Dell, named by no CHGR. Dell divergence reconstructed entirely from local Git objects with zero Dell access of any kind: Dell is pinned at 28bf137b5dc95d024e8913b678dce0501a46fd0f (78 commits behind HEAD), where both producer files are absent, HBDC-001 is v1.0, HMIC-001 is v1.3 and frozen membership is 28. Boundary-P status preserved as INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED PHYSICAL PROVISIONING (149O.20L.7E); source currency is a separate axis and is now stale on Dell. Live-HBDC wording is version-qualified: Dell currently executes the HBDC-001 v1.0-era deployed source; it is not claimed that Dell executes HBDC-001 v1.1. Future redeployment is noted as a prerequisite for any first use and was not performed, prepared, or authorized. Certification consequence: none -- no HMIC certification exists on any host, so a source-scope amendment has no live revocation consequence. First use remains unauthorized: no registry.json, repository-identity.json, deployment-binding.json, certifications.json, certification-bindings.json or active-certification.json exists in this repository or in the production trust-store root (which does not exist), and no decision session, first-use CHGR, RepositoryIdentity, DeploymentBinding, election, or certification exists.
